    - The cliff's in the song now. You can hear the gulls in the second bar if you listen. You won't, but you could.
    - I played your dawn last night. Bethoc cried. Bethoc never cries. Well, she said it was the onions.
    - A request? I'll play it faster than you want. Fair warning.
        - *Choice:* Who are you?

    - Mhairi, fiddler of the Gap Inn and the race send-off. My da made my first fiddle from a mast offcut when I was seven. It squeaked on every note. It's on my wall still.
    - Cormac taught me the old tunes when I could barely hold the bow. He said a tune is a story you can dance to. Now I play them faster than he can sing them, to make him laugh.
    - A verse for the gap at dawn, one for Iska at the tiller, one for Tamsin hammering on the slip all winter, and a rowdy one for Jory that he keeps asking me to make longer.
    - No last verse. The last verse is the finish, and I won't write the Gap Runner losing. So Goa has to win. I've told the whole inn. The crew love me for it. Some days.
    - Sometimes Cormac starts that old gap verse and stops after one line, and his face goes still. I don't like it. I play something quick after, and he laughs, and that's better.
    - Off you go! Feet first.
